topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus, Democratic Republic of the Congo
date_evidence: Citable reference: World Health Organization (1 August 2026). Disease Outbreak News; Bundibugyo Virus Disease, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
key_claim: The Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in DRC is the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the country, with 3605 confirmed cases and 1587 deaths (CFR 44%) as of 30 July 2026 across 49 health zones in five provinces.
frame_summary: WHO argues the response is being outpaced by the outbreak and that a substantial scale-up across all response pillars, not travel or trade restrictions, is what is needed to get ahead of it.
verbatim_quote: As of 30 July 2026, a total of 3605 confirmed cases, including 1587 deaths (CFR 44%), have been reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
verbatim_list: Ituri remains the most affected province, accounting for 88% (3176/3605) of all confirmed cases and 82.6% (1311/1587) of reported deaths nationwide.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
publisher: World Health Organization (Disease Outbreak News, DRC and Uganda)
title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus, Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda
date_evidence: Citable reference: World Health Organization (17 July 2026). Disease Outbreak News; Bundibugyo Virus Disease, Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.
key_claim: As of 15 July 2026 the DRC had 2124 confirmed cases and 828 deaths, with 119 confirmed infections among health workers at a 30.3% case fatality ratio, while Uganda began its 42-day countdown after its last case on 21 June.
frame_summary: WHO argues that occupational exposure, weak infection prevention in health facilities and conflict-driven population movement are the conditions sustaining transmission, and that response must be community-led rather than externally imposed.
verbatim_quote: Infections among health workers continued to increase, with 119 confirmed cases, 61 recoveries and 36 deaths reported among health workers, corresponding to a CFR of 30.3%.
verbatim_list: Since 3 July 2026, an additional 664 confirmed cases, including 376 confirmed deaths, have been reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

date_evidence:
WHO Member States agree to extend negotiations on Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing annex

1 May 2026

News release
key_claim: Member states could not finalise the PABS annex and agreed to extend negotiations, with the outcome due to the May 2027 Assembly or an earlier special session, leaving the Pandemic Agreement unable to open for signature.
frame_summary: WHO frames the delay as progress requiring more time rather than failure, arguing that the annex is the last piece needed before countries can ratify the Pandemic Agreement.
verbatim_quote: Given the need for further negotiations, the Assembly will be asked to consider continuing IGWG’s work as mandated in Resolution WHA78.1 and submit the outcome to the next Assembly in May 2027, or earlier by a special session of WHA in 2026.

title: 10 Year Capital Plan to rebuild NHS and bring care closer to home
key_claim: England's 10 Year Capital Plan commits a health capital budget rising to £15 billion in 2029/30, confirms 250 Neighbourhood Health Centres, and allocates at least £6.75 billion over nine years to repairs and the maintenance backlog.
frame_summary: DHSC argues that replacing stop-start investment with a long-term capital settlement is what makes the neighbourhood care model deliverable rather than aspirational.

title: Critical medicines act: Council and Parliament reach provisional deal
date_evidence: Council of the EU - Press release - 12 May 2026 06:02
key_claim: The Council and Parliament reached a provisional deal on the Critical Medicines Act, adding resilience requirements to public procurement, cutting the joint-procurement threshold from nine member states to five, and extending scope to orphan medicines, with formal adoption still pending.
frame_summary: The Council argues that procurement rules and EU-based manufacturing incentives are the practical route to reducing dependency and ending shortages of antibiotics, insulin and painkillers.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
publisher: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health (IVAC, global immunization)
title: Latest Global Immunization Coverage Estimates Illustrate Gaps in Vaccine Access
key_claim: WHO and UNICEF estimates show global immunisation coverage was broadly flat in 2025, with 13.5 million zero-dose children and measles first-dose coverage stalled at 84% against a 95% target.
frame_summary: IVAC argues that flat coverage combined with falling global health financing puts immunisation targets out of reach, and that zero-dose children in fragile settings need different strategies rather than more of the same.
verbatim_quote: An estimated 13.5 million zero-dose children did not receive their first dose of DTP vaccine in 2025, approximately 750,000 fewer children than 2024, but far too many children continue to miss out on life-saving vaccines.
verbatim_list: Measles vaccine coverage has also stalled, with only 84% of children receiving their first dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) and just 77% receiving their second dose.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: Measles Elimination Status: What It Is and How the U.S. Could Lose It
key_claim: The US reported over 3,800 measles cases between January 2025 and March 2026, with 48 outbreaks in 2025 and 16 more by March 2026, against 64 outbreaks across the whole decade to 2011.
frame_summary: KFF argues that losing elimination status would matter less as a technical reclassification than as a marker of eroded US commitment to measles prevention, foreshadowing endemic transmission and recurring costs.
verbatim_quote: There were 64 measles outbreaks in total over ten years (2001 -2011) but in 2025 there were 48 outbreaks, and there have been 16 new outbreaks in 2026 through March.
verbatim_list: However, a series of measles outbreaks began in the U.S. in early 2025 that continue today: from January 2025 through the end of March 2026, U.S. states have reported over 3,800 measles cases.

title: What to Know About the BALANCE Model for GLP-1s in Medicare and Medicaid and the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge
key_claim: CMS delayed the BALANCE Model indefinitely after Part D sponsor uptake fell short of an 80% participation threshold, extending the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge instead at a $245 net monthly price through the end of 2027.
frame_summary: KFF argues that GLP-1 access rests on fragile temporary demonstration authority rather than statutory entitlement, leaving beneficiaries facing a coverage cliff and payers unwilling to absorb unquantified cost risk.
verbatim_quote: Manufacturers have agreed to provide eligible GLP-1s under the Bridge program at a net price of $245 per month supply.
verbatim_list: CMS was aiming for a “critical mass” of Part D sponsors to participate and established a threshold participation rate of 80% for 2027.

key_claim: The proclamation imposes a 100 percent ad valorem duty on imported patented pharmaceuticals and their ingredients, reduced to 20 percent for companies with approved onshoring plans and to zero for companies holding MFN pricing agreements, effective 31 July 2026 for Annex III companies and 29 September 2026 for the rest, with generics excluded.
frame_summary: The proclamation asserts that heavy US import reliance on patented pharmaceuticals and ingredients, compounded by foreign government intervention in the market, threatens to impair national security, and that tariffs paired with onshoring and pricing agreements are the remedy.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: Trump signs executive order to break up measles, mumps, rubella vaccine
date_evidence: President Donald Trump signs an Executive Order on vaccines on Aug. 10, 2026.
key_claim: An executive order signed on 10 August 2026 urges childhood vaccines to be given at separate visits and calls for the MMR vaccine to be split into three, directing the attorney general to act against state vaccine laws, while at least 23 states now follow AAP rather than CDC guidance.
frame_summary: CIDRAP argues the order is not evidence-based, would raise cost and infection risk without licensed separate vaccines existing, and adds confusion at a point when measles is spreading and children are returning to school.
verbatim_quote: The order advises states and territories to consider updating their vaccine laws and regulations, and it directs the attorney general to take legal action against states with laws that violate religious freedom, disability accommodations, or parental authority.
verbatim_list: But public health experts worry that the order will create more confusion for parents.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: EXCLUSIVE: Here is the 'Final Text' of UN Political Declaration on Pandemics, Although its Adoption is Far From Guaranteed
key_claim: The final text of the UN Political Declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response went under silence procedure on 28 July ahead of a 25 September High-Level Meeting, but omits concrete timelines for the $15 billion needed annually for preparedness.
frame_summary: The piece argues the declaration names every problem and commits to none of the fixes, and that the fight over it will turn on ideological objections rather than on the missing implementation and financing plan.
verbatim_quote: The first weakness is the lack of “concrete commitments or timelines” to fill the financing gap, including the $15 billion needed annually to prepare for pandemics.
verbatim_list: The HLM is set for 25 September, the last Friday of the UN General Assembly.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: How well are AI-discovered drugs faring in the clinic?
key_claim: Few AI-discovered drugs have reached late-stage trials, with Insilico's rentosertib now in a 52-week phase 3 in China and Recursion posting a polyp-burden reduction, set against failures such as Verge Genomics' ALS candidate.
frame_summary: The piece argues that AI's apparent early-phase advantage remains unproven where it matters, and that the technology's real test is whether a small number of closely watched assets survive mid-stage and late-stage efficacy trials.
verbatim_quote: Insilico also has its own candidates in the works as part of an expansive pipeline that includes over 40 programs in a wide swath of indications.
verbatim_list: Most patients in the trial continued to show reductions even after they were off the medication for 12 weeks — a promising sign for a condition with no existing treatment options.
